name: Fit a straight line
summary: Fit y = slope*x + intercept by ordinary least squares and report Pearson r.
description: Fit a line with an intercept to paired finite numeric lists x and y of equal length. Return count, slope, intercept and Pearson correlation r. Constant x is rejected because the line is not identifiable. For constant y and nonconstant x, return slope 0, intercept equal to that constant and r null (undefined correlation). Duplicate x values are allowed if x is not entirely constant. The computation normalizes numeric scales before using standard-library regression and correlation, then transforms the line back. Outputs are rounded floating-point values. No code, files or expressions are accepted.
limitations: 2 to 10000 finite numbers per list, equal lengths, each number between -1e12 and 1e12 inclusive. Booleans, numeric strings and expressions are rejected.
Constant x is not identifiable and is rejected; constant y has r null. No missing-value filtering is performed.
Outputs use binary floating point; results outside finite floating-point range are rejected, and rounding or underflow may affect extreme scales.
This is a descriptive OLS fit with an intercept, not a causal finding, uncertainty estimate or significance test.

failure_modes.condition: Invalid lists, unequal lengths or constant x.
failure_modes.recovery: Supply bounded paired observations with at least two distinct x values.

failure_modes.condition: The fitted result exceeds finite floating-point range.
failure_modes.symptom: Capability error; no infinite result is returned.
failure_modes.recovery: Rescale the numeric observations and state the units used.
